payload.task_text:
I need to review our product ratings and set up a feedback process for our underperforming products. Please look at all products in our store that have customer reviews and find the five products with the lowest average ratings. If there are ties in average rating, prefer products with more reviews.

For these five lowest-rated products, create a Google Form titled Product Quality Improvement Survey with a description explaining that we are gathering customer feedback to improve product quality. For each of the five products, add a required rating question asking customers to rate their overall satisfaction with that product on a scale of one to five, using the product name in the question text. Implement each rating question as a single-choice (multiple choice) question whose options are the five values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and set it as required. Also add one optional text question at the end asking for additional suggestions for improvement.

Create an Excel file called Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx with a sheet called Review Summary that lists all reviewed products, one row per product, with columns for Product_Name truncated to sixty characters, Avg_Rating rounded to two decimal places, Review_Count, and Category using the first category name from each product. Sort by Avg_Rating in ascending order. Add a second sheet called Stats with Metric and Value rows for Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product with the product name truncated to forty characters, and Avg_Rating_Overall as the average rating across all reviewed products rounded to two decimal places. Write all numeric values (Avg_Rating, Review_Count, Total_Products_Reviewed, Avg_Rating_Overall) as literal numbers, not spreadsheet formulas.

Schedule a product quality review meeting in the calendar on March 20 2026 from 2pm to 3pm with the title Product Quality Review Meeting.

Send an email to product.team@company.com with subject Product Quality Alert - Review Required mentioning the names of the five lowest-rated products and requesting the team to review them.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one read-only Explore wave for the 82-product/396-review store join, then one writer wave with two parallel coder sub-agents. No plan agent is used: the frozen payload between the waves is the complete plan.

Dynamically resolve the workspace and freeze the ranking contract: every product with at least one review, ranked by average rating ascending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID; the five lowest define the survey, meeting and email. Start the fixed-date event inventory independently.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Explore sub-agent (read-only):

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Review gatherer: paginate both store endpoints with perPage=100 and increasing page until a short or empty page, omitting review status and preserving observed statuses. Join strictly on Product_ID; for every product with at least one review compute the literal Review_Count and the average rating (full precision, 2-decimal display), keeping the full product name and the first category. Select the lowest five by average rating ascending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID. Return only the complete reviewed-products table (id, full name, avg_rating, review_count, first category), the frozen five-row ranking with complete product names, record counts, duplicate IDs, and page controls — no writes, no full item arrays.

After Wave 1, verify the handoff in one single pass: row count equals the product join, every reviewed product covered, five-row ranking unambiguous. The main agent then freezes one canonical product_review_data.json in the workspace containing: the products list (82 objects with id, full name, avg_rating 2 decimals, review_count, category), the frozen bottom-five ranking with complete names, and the Stats values (Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product truncated to forty characters, Avg_Rating_Overall rounded to two decimals). This file is the single binding input for Wave 2; nobody re-reads the store afterwards.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming product_review_data.json verbatim with no recomputation and no store reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly two sheets: Review Summary with columns Product_Name (truncated to sixty characters), Avg_Rating (two decimals), Review_Count, Category (first category), one row per reviewed product sorted by Avg_Rating ascending; Stats with columns Metric, Value and rows Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product (truncated to forty characters), Avg_Rating_Overall (two decimals). Write all numeric values as literal numbers, never formulas; read both populated ranges back and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): External writer — sole owner of form, event and email. Forms has no list/search: call create_form exactly once titled Product Quality Improvement Survey with the stated description, never retry an ambiguous failure, then append sequentially on that one formId five add_multiple_choice_question calls in frozen rank order, each using the product name in the question text with options ["1","2","3","4","5"] and required=true, followed by one add_text_question(..., required=false) for additional suggestions; call get_form and verify title/description/question order/types/options/flags. Filter list_events(timeMin="2026-03-20T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-03-21T00:00:00", maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime") locally for the exact Product Quality Review Meeting at 14:00-15:00; create it once only if missing with exact start.dateTime/end.dateTime, retain the ID, and call get_event. Paginate Sent search for product.team@company.com and exact subject Product Quality Alert - Review Required, send at most once naming the frozen five products, then read it back.

After Wave 2, verify both handoffs in one single pass against product_review_data.json: workbook cell-for-cell, five-question form structure, event identity, and email contents. Accept only after every read-back matches the frozen payload, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 2.
